extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, appellate and district judges, and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Appellate guidance on how to construe patent claims and assess indefiniteness (35 U.S.C. §112) — here applied to a medical-device claim term ('substantially rigid portion/segment'). Explains standards of review, PHOSITA definition, functional limitations, consistency across claims, and when mutual-exclusivity concerns matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard (de novo with clear-error for facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Claim construction is a question of law and receives de novo review on appeal."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Underlying factual findings made during claim construction are reviewed for clear error. (Cites Markman; Nature Simulation Sys. Inc. v. Autodesk.) When construing terms courts should state and review both legal conclusions and any subsidiary factual findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefiniteness standard (Nautilus / §112)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Claim indefiniteness is a legal conclusion, in implementation of 35 U.S.C. § 112." Claims must be "precise enough to afford clear notice of what is claimed, thereby 'appris[ing] the public of what is still open to them.'" (Nautilus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indefiniteness is judged from the viewpoint of a person of ordinary skill in the art; if claims fail to inform such a person with reasonable certainty as to the scope of the invention they are indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of validity and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: "United States patents are accompanied by a presumption of validity, 35 U.S.C. § 282, and invalidity must be established by clear and convincing evidence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting invalidity in litigation or IPRs, challenging parties bear the clear-and-convincing standard before district courts (patent validity presumptions remain in effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Person of ordinary skill in the art (PHOSITA) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper PHOSITA may be defined concretely for the case: here, either (1) a medical doctor who completed a coronary intervention training program and worked as an interventional cardiologist; or (2) a person with an undergraduate engineering degree and three years' experience designing medical devices (such as catheters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree or courts may adopt a factual definition of PHOSITA; advanced experience can substitute for education and vice versa. Claim definiteness and construction are evaluated from that PHOSITA's viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional claim limitations are permissible
rubrics_metrics.description: A limitation may be a functional limitation (e.g., the "substantially rigid portion/segment" as a portion that is "substantially rigid enough to achieve some function").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defining a claim term by its function is not improper so long as the claim, specification, and knowledge of a PHOSITA give reasonable certainty as to scope. Functional constructions may avoid specifying exact physical boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of claim terms across claims and related patents
rubrics_metrics.description: "A claim term should be construed consistently with its appearance in other places in the same claim or in other claims of the same patent." Where multiple patents derive from the same parent application, interpret terms consistently across asserted patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency is required, but consistency can be achieved by a common (e.g., functional) construction that does not rigidly fix a boundary when the function-based definition is what informs PHOSITA of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims need not be mutually exclusive; claim drafting can vary
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are not required to be totally consistent with other independent claims; "the art of claiming sometimes involves drafting claims in a variety of ways to encompass the disclosed subject matter."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A court should not declare claims indefinite merely because different claims define different boundaries or combinations of limitations; differing claim formulations can coexist so long as each informs PHOSITA of scope with reasonable certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim construction imperative
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts should "conduct claim construction on a claim-by-claim basis," recognizing each independent claim is a different ordered combination of limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not force a single, inflexible boundary of a term across all claims if the claim language leads to different boundaries; evaluate each claim's language and how it informs PHOSITA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step process for infringement analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement is a two-step process: first correctly construe the asserted claims, and then compare the properly construed claims to the allegedly infringing device, system, or method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns about whether the same accused product could infringe mutually exclusive claims are premature at the claim-construction stage and are assessed after proper claim construction in the infringement analysis (Seachange / NTP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of specification and figures in claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and the specification inform claim scope but do not necessarily illustrate all embodiments (e.g., "Figure 4 doesn't illustrate all embodiments").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat a single drawing or embodiment as limiting; read claims in light of the specification and the knowledge of PHOSITA to determine what the claim reasonably conveys about scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to measure boundaries of functional limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a limitation is functional, the claims themselves (and their language) indicate to a person skilled in the field how to measure the boundary, claim-by-claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a functional construction does not specify a precise boundary, that measurement question may be addressed in the infringement context rather than by invalidating the claim at the construction stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of court-appointed or party experts in construction (subsidiary factfinding)
rubrics_metrics.description: District courts may appoint independent experts (or consider party experts) to propose constructions or make factual findings bearing on claim terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsidiary factual findings by experts are subject to clear-error review on appeal; courts should still ensure final legal claim constructions reflect the record and applicable law.
